Commentary.Commentary: Will South Africa be able to defend the total or will Australia chase it easily? Join us for the run chase in a bit.

On the other hand, South Africa started off with a bang where Quinton de Kock and Reeza Hendricks were attacking the bowlers. Hendricks did not last long and got out. De Kock played a fine innings for his 70 and Rassie van der Dussen also played an excellent hand for his 37. David Miller also struggled throughout his innings and was not able to play big shots.

It has been an excellent display of bowling from Australia in the last five overs. They bowled cutters and the slower ones and did not allow the South African batsmen to play big shots. Kane Richardson was the most economical bowler and he picked two wickets.

Full delivery on off, Biljon lofts it over covers. Steven Smith in the deep takes the catch but loses his balance. He throws the ball in play before going over the ropes but could not take it after coming inside. The batsmen get two runs. SOUTH AFRICA FINISH WITH 158/4!

OUT! CAUGHT! Full delivery outside off, du Plessis looks to loft it over covers but gets a top edge. It goes towards covers where Kane Richardson takes a simple catch. De Kock needs someone to hang around with him. He is single-handedly hurting Australia.

Defended off the back foot by the batsman.

Loopy delivery on middle, de Kock plays a slog sweep over fine leg. The fielder chases it and does well to stop it just before the ropes. The batsmen take a single. End of the Powerplay. South Africa are 59/0 after 6 overs.
SIX! That is huge! Flighted delivery on middle, de Kock lofts it over the bowler's head for a maximum.

It is a bird, it is a plane. Nay, it is Superman Steve! Unbelievable effort. No soul apart from this bloke thought that is anything less than 6. Short and outside off, de Kock rocks back and pulls. The ball has the trajectory, it seems. It is travelling into the crowd but out of nowhere, Steven Smith rushes to his left at deep mid-wicket, flings himself in the air, stretches out his left hand, takes the catch, realizes that he is going over the ropes and parries it back into play! FOUR! FLAMBOYANT! Full and outside off, de Kock walks into the shot and drives it through mid off!

Fine comeback by the bowler, an inswinging yorker, de Kock is beaten by the length, as he looks to flick and is hit on the right boot. There is an LBW appeal but it is turned down. Missing leg stump.

WIDE. Down the leg side, flick shot missed.

Good start from Starc. Right on the money. Full and around off, hint of outswing, watchfully pushed towards point.
The players are out in the middle. Reeza Hendricks and Quinton de Kock are the openers for South Africa. Mitchell Starc to start off proceedings against de Kock. Here we go...

Australian captain, Aaron Finch, admits that the bowlers did reasonably well in the first game and expects nothing different this time. On the possibility of his side peaking too early for the upcoming T20 World Cup, Finch brushes that aside and simply states that it is a nice feeling to have your players do well. Agrees with de Kock that the pitch looks a lot drier than the one in Jo'burg and expects turn later on.

South African skipper, Quinton de Kock, says that the wicket looks dry but firm and should not change too much for the game. Expects it to slow down a touch in the second innings. On the recovery from the previous game, de Kock says that everyone is mentally fine. Informs that there are three changes to the side. Stresses that Reeza Hendricks replaces JJ Smuts, Dwaine Pretorius comes in for Andile Phehlukwayo while Anrich Nortje replaces Dale Steyn. On the possibility of dropping Rassie van der Dussen down the order, Quinton says that it is a logical change, with Reeza Hendricks ready to slot in for the opening spot. Is super excited to have Reeza back, stating that he has been in excellent form in the domestic season.

Australia (UNCHANGED Playing XI) - David Warner, Aaron Finch (C), Steven Smith, Matthew Wade, Mitchell Marsh, Alex Carey (WK), Ashton Agar, Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Kane Richardson and Adam Zampa.

South Africa (Playing XI) - Quinton de Kock (C AND WK), Reeza Hendricks (IN FOR JJ SMUTS), Faf du Plessis, Rassie van der Dussen, David Miller, Pite van Biljon, Dwaine Pretorius (IN FOR ANDILE PHEHLUKWAYO), Kagiso Rabada, Anrich Nortje (IN FOR DALE STEYN), Lungi Ngidi and Tabraiz Shamsi.
TOSS - The news from out in the middle is that Quinton de Kock has won the toss yet again. SOUTH AFRICA WILL BAT FIRST this time.

Friday, the 21st. Almost as if it never existed for South Africa. They bowled badly, fielded poorly and batted miserably. On a positive note, they would look at it as all bad things happening in one single game and the next can be nowhere lower - so the only place is to go up. Today might be that day. Hello and a warm welcome to the second T20I between South Africa and Australia in Port Elizabeth.
